h: The Sweet Sleep of Atzeres: Ta'amei Torah Given in a Dream

p: This is a blessing over the Torah,
that he has already been exempted with Ahavah Rabbah.
whose attribute was the attribute of love —
the two thousand years of Torah
for he was a lover of Hashem Yisbarach,
and consequently through this he merited
that Hashem Yisbarach loved him too;
so is the heart of man to man"
is expounded in the Sifrei (Sifrei, Devarim 24)
as applying also to Hashem Yisbarach.
"And from Your love with which You loved him," etc.
This is as it is said
"Is not Esav a brother to Yaakov,
that is, love without a reason:
even if Yaakov, chas v'shalom, acts
Because the sleep of Atzeres is sweet
it says that for this reason
we stay awake the entire night,
But the word "sweet" does not imply
that there was some flaw or sin in this
אִם ה׳ לֹא יִבְנֶה בַיִת וְגוֹ׳
"If Hashem does not build the house," etc.;
"It is vain for you who rise early,
who eat the bread of toil;
so He gives His beloved sleep."
and there is "the bread of toil,"
meaning that the words of Torah
come with labor, toil and pain.
And about Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him,
To him was transmitted all the lower wisdom,
in one night, in a dream;
and about this it is said,
of whom it is written, "yet I loved Yaakov" —
"and behold, Hashem stood over him," etc.,
for the revelation was revealed to him
regarding Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
for he merited the words of Torah
that Hashem loved him as well.
that everything is from Hashem Yisbarach
and nothing comes from his own effort.
Therefore he merited in a dream,
that the fear of Hashem falls upon one
automatically and of its own accord.
meaning that he pictures before himself
and through this it falls upon him
the fear and awe fall upon him
"The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem,"
"Behold, the fear of Hashem is wisdom" —
and to taste flavor in the words of Torah.
And this is the essence and foundation
to sense flavor in the words of Torah.
"This is one who reveals the things
that the Ancient of Days concealed."
to taste and sense a sweet flavor
And this he merited in a dream,
that when they would afterward receive the Torah,
there would be fixed in them
that is, that there would be fixed in them
awe and longing for the words of Torah;
and this is "the beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem."
And from this comes the light of Torah,
to sense light and sweetness in the heart
and this was transmitted to them in sleep.
And this is what the Midrash says:
the longing and the permanence in the heart
the light of Torah she'b'al peh.
And night is the time of Torah she'b'al peh,
When HaKadosh Baruch Hu was teaching him
he knew that it was day;
and when He was teaching him orally
he knew that it was night, etc.
For day corresponds to the Name Havayah,
the aspect of the Written Torah,
and night corresponds to the Name Adnus,
the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh.
"For Hashem Elokim is a sun and a shield";
and the moon receives from the sun,
receives the light from the Written Torah.
And so it says in the holy Zohar
the eve of the three days, etc.,
are the seventy facets of the Torah;
there are seventy in the Sanhedrin,
seventy opinions in the words of Torah.
And this matches the number of the seventy nations,
which must be extracted from them
And the opinions in the words of Torah
And the Name Adnus signifies awe,
And it is the attribute of Malchus, the mouth,
And this they merited on the night
and this is the meaning of the Midrash,
that "the sleep of Atzeres is sweet."

paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah 9a — "It was taught in the school of Eliyahu: The world is to exist for six thousand years: two thousand years of tohu, two thousand years of Torah, two thousand years the days of Mashiach." The Gemara reckons the two thousand years of Torah from Avraham's time in Charan.

paragraphs.text: Sifrei, Devarim 24 — "'Because Hashem hated us' (Devarim 1:27): is it possible that the Omnipresent hates Israel? Has it not already been said, 'I have loved you, says Hashem' (Malachi 1:2)? Rather, it is they who hated the Omnipresent. paragraphs.text: Magen Avraham, Orach Chaim 494 (introduction) — "The Zohar writes that the early pious ones would stay awake all night on Shavuos and occupy themselves with Torah; and the reason is, as is said in the Midrash, that Israel slept all that night and the Holy One had to wake them, as it says, 'Why did I come, and there was no man?' (Yeshayahu 50:2); therefore we must rectify this."

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 119a — "What is 'and for covering the Ancient (mechaseh atik)' (Yeshayahu 23:18)? This is one who covers the things that the Ancient of Days covered — and what are they? The secrets of the Torah. And some say: this is one who reveals the things that the Ancient of Days covered — and what are they? The reasons of the Torah." Rashi: the secrets are Maaseh Merkavah and Maaseh Bereishis.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Va'era 6 — “The Zohar (II 166b): this light the Holy One sowed in His Garden of Eden… and the first light is destined to bring forth offspring for the World to Come… even every day, for were it not for this light the world could not stand… The world was created through the Torah, as it says, ‘I was His instrument’; and afterward, in His goodness He renews each day the work of creation through the renewal of halachos that the Holy One renews each day, and after Matan Torah it was given over to the Sages.” Connection: Both passages treat the theme “the hidden light is revealed to those who toil in the Oral Torah.”

paragraphs.text: Bava Kamma 17a — “Rabbi Yochanan said in Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai’s name: What is meant by ‘Happy are you who sow beside all waters, sending forth the foot of the ox and the donkey’? Whoever engages in Torah and acts of kindness merits the inheritance of two tribes. ... ‘Sowing’ means charity, as it is written, ‘Sow for yourselves in righteousness and reap according to kindness’; ‘water’ means Torah, as it is written, ‘All who are thirsty, come to the water.’” The identification of water with Torah supplies the basis for Rav Tzadok’s further distinction between the visibly descending rain and the less apparent arrival of dew.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 80b (Kedoshim) — "A person is never purified except through the words of Torah; therefore words of Torah do not receive impurity, for it stands to purify the impure… And purity is found in the Torah, as it is written, 'The fear of Hashem is pure, enduring forever' (Tehillim 19:10). What is 'enduring forever'? That it stands constantly in that purity and never departs from it."
